releases.summary: Space between items and animation speed are now settings — site-wide under Appearance, and per block in its Design tab. Left empty, every block keeps what it was drawn with, so nothing changes until you ask it to.

Status and chart colours, and the text sizes inside blocks, are now yours to change — with the values that were already compiled in as the defaults, so nothing moves. The words inside blocks can be translated at last.

A card grid now has a Space between cards field — a different thing from a card’s own margin, which only shifts that card inside its cell. Left empty, each layout keeps the spacing it was designed with.

Cards can be styled one at a time — background, text colour, spacing, border, radius, alignment — on every card layout. And a heading with its subtitle beside it can line the two halves up at the top, centred or at the bottom instead of always centring them.

npm run release:merge now finishes after a conflict. It told you to merge by hand and run it again, then stopped because there was nothing left to merge — so it never checked or tagged. Only relevant to sites kept in their own repository.

Line breaks you type in Body, Intro and Description fields now appear on the page. They were being collapsed, so text ran together with nothing in the editor to say so. Fixed for every block rather than one at a time.

Fixes the test suite failing in the public repository. The licence test added in 2.6.1 read files that repository does not carry, so it was red over a licence that was correct. A guard now stops a test shipping that cannot pass where it lands.

The engine is now MIT licensed. It was published with no licence at all, which legally meant all rights reserved. The bundled typefaces keep their own licences, which the notice states rather than glossing over.

Typography size, weight, colour and letter spacing now show the block’s real values — and stay silent where a section’s headings genuinely differ, rather than naming one of them. Measured against your saved theme rather than the shipped defaults.

Background colour, border widths, border colour and corner radius now show the block’s real values instead of “inherit” — and the fields that genuinely inherit nothing, like an overlay or a gradient stop, now say none.

Fixes the block spacing added in 2.2.0, which never appeared: the browser was refusing to load the page the panel measures, and a refusal looks exactly like a feature that does not work. The Design tab now shows each block’s real padding and margin.

One command — npm run release:merge — takes a release into a site that has changes of its own, and refuses to tag anything it cannot verify: a conflicted merge, a wrong version, or a merge that quietly replaced a file you had changed.

Updating is safer. An update now proves the release is the version it claims, and refuses to check one out over commits your own site has — your ports, your process name — instead of replacing them and reporting success. Release tags can no longer collide with your own.

A block’s Design tab now shows the spacing it already has, per screen size, instead of leaving you to guess what a value would replace. Measured from the block itself rather than read from a list, so it stays true as blocks change.

Fixes an update that finished but could never say so. The reload restarts the process writing the record, so the panel sat on “reload…” for ever and refused every later update. It now settles such a run from the version actually running, and always offers a way to clear one.

Write your own CSS — for the whole site, or for one page — and switch on Google Analytics with a measurement id. Saving a page now shows the change straight away: three caches were holding the old one, and there is a Clear cache button for when one still does.

Fixes updating: the update now finds your site’s process instead of assuming it is called “engine”, stops on a failed migration instead of rebuilding anyway, and adds npm run db:status. No database changes.

Your site can speak more than one language, advertise jobs and take applications. Fifty-five more typefaces, including Armenian. What visitors send is now deleted after a period rather than kept for ever.
Export a site's content — pages, posts, media and design — and import it into another site. No accounts and no visitor data travel with it.
Three more roles — manager, author and reviewer — alongside administrator and editor. Existing accounts are unchanged.
The first release: block builder, templates, sliders, forms, popups, email, security, backups, and a browser installer that writes its own configuration.
